title: Dead-letter
description: Event deliveries @gnldev/events gave up on. A topic fans out, so an event that keeps failing is quarantined per consumer — pick the topic and the consumer, then release the ones that should be delivered again. Releasing updates the record in place; it does not re-emit the event to healthy consumers.
loadTitle: Scan this topic's log for quarantined deliveries
scanCostHelp: This reads the whole topic log, so it runs only when you ask — nothing on this page refreshes on a timer.
pickTitle: Choose a topic and a consumer
pickDescription: A dead-letter record belongs to one consumer, not to the topic: the same event can be quarantined for one consumer and delivered fine to another. There is no combined list to show.
emptyDescription: Every delivery either succeeded or is still within its retry budget. A quarantine only appears after a handler has failed its maximum number of attempts, spread over roughly two hours by the retry schedule.
disabledDescription: It appears once your app passes the `events` option to Studio, wrapping @gnldev/events' listDeadEvents / retryDeadEvent over its own WorkStore.
detailsShow: Show the full error and the event body
payloadRestricted: Event bodies are hidden for your account. They hold whatever the producer emitted — customer data — so they need the `payloads:read` permission, which the rest of this page does not.
errorRestricted: The handler's error text is hidden for your account. It is written by your own handler while it runs on the event body, so it routinely quotes it — which puts it behind the same `payloads:read` permission as the body. The rest of the row still shows how much is stuck and whether releasing it has helped; your server logs record the failure in full.
releaseTitle: Hand this event back to this consumer with a fresh attempt budget
releaseAgainTitle: Already released but never rescanned — an in-flight poll can swallow the rescan flag, and re-asserting the release is the way out
